lines.text: Today you will make boxes line up side by side, like the cards on your favourite apps.
A class is a name you give to some elements, like class equals card.
In CSS, a dot in front of the name picks every element with that class.
Now you can style some paragraphs without changing all of them.
The div tag is a plain box with no special meaning.
We use it to group things together so we can style or move them as one.
Cards and rows are usually divs with a class.
Put display flex on a parent box, and its children line up in a row.
The gap property adds equal space between the boxes.
Flex-wrap lets cards move to a new line when the screen is narrow.
A card is a box with padding, a border and rounded corners from border-radius.
A white card on a coloured background really stands out.
Apps like video and shopping sites use cards everywhere.
Only the paragraphs with class big get the large font.
In CSS we write a dot before the class name, but in HTML there is no dot.
Normally every div starts on a new line, so the boxes stack like plates.
To put them side by side, we need flexbox.
We wrap the cards in a row div, then give the row display flex.
The children line up side by side, and gap adds the space between them.
Border radius rounds the corners, and padding gives the words room to breathe.
Now it looks like a real app.
Two small mistakes are hiding in this code. Can you find them?
The CSS needs a dot before card, and the HTML class should not have a dot.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
